library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gastine_2019_micafungin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gastine_2019_micafungin"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-53093-6>

# Population

Gastine 2019 studied 36 critically ill adults (24 male, 12 female; median age
65 years, range 22-84; median weight 94.5 kg, range 49.9-162) in the intensive
care units of the University Hospital Muenster, Germany. All received
micafungin 100 mg intravenously once daily as empirical (25 patients) or
targeted (11 patients) therapy of suspected or proven Candida infection. The
cohort was severely ill: APACHE II median 35, SOFA median 12 (range 2-22),
SAPS II median 55; 78% met sepsis criteria, 75% received vasopressors, 86% were
mechanically ventilated, 16% were on ECMO and 64% (23/36) received renal
replacement therapy (CVVHDF, SLEDD or intermittent haemodialysis) on at least
one study day (Table 1). On day 1 plasma was sampled at 1, 4, 8, 12, 16 and
20 h and before the next dose; from day 2 a peak and a trough were taken daily.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Gastine_2019_micafungin")$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them with the model equations.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2 compartments, linear elimination, IV input | -- | Results 'Population pharmacokinetic modelling'; Methods (ADVAN6, FOCE-I) |
| `lcl` (CL at SOFA 12, bilirubin <= 4 mg/dL) | log(1.56) L/h | Table 2, Clearance 1.56 (RSE 4.8%) |
| `lvc` (Vc at SOFA <= 10) | log(16.2) L | Table 2, Central volume 16.2 (RSE 12.7%) |
| `lq` (Q) | log(14.4) L/h | Table 2, Inter-compartmental clearance 14.4 (RSE 7.7%) |
| `lvp` (Vp) | log(13.8) L | Table 2, Peripheral volume 13.8 (RSE 15.7%) |
| `e_sofa_cl`: `CL x (1 + e_sofa_cl x (SOFA - 12))` | -0.024 per point | Results: 'linear decrease in clearance with a factor of 0.024 per score point'; centring on the Table 1 median 12 (see Assumptions) |
| `e_sofa_vc`: `Vc x (1 + e_sofa_vc)` if SOFA > 10 | -0.308 | Results and Abstract: 30.8% lower Vc with SOFA > 10 |
| `e_tbili_cl`: `CL x (1 + e_tbili_cl)` if bilirubin > 4 mg/dL | -0.211 | Results and Abstract: 21.1% lower CL with bilirubin > 4 mg/dL |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.259^2) | Table 2, IIV clearance 25.9% |
| `etalvc` | log(1 + 0.489^2) | Table 2, IIV central volume 48.9% |
| `etalvp` | log(1 + 0.70^2) | Table 2, IIV peripheral volume 70% |
| `propSd` | 0.257 | Table 2, Proportional residual error 0.257 |
| Dose | 100 mg once daily IV | Methods 'Study protocol' |

# Virtual cohort

Table 1 gives the SOFA distribution only as a median and range (12; 2-22), and
the paper does not report the bilirubin distribution. The cohort below draws a
per-subject SOFA score from a normal distribution with mean 12 and SD 4,
rounded and truncated to 2-22, and holds bilirubin at 1 mg/dL (17.1 umol/L,
below the 4 mg/dL threshold) for everyone. The covariates are held constant
over the simulated week, whereas the study re-scored SOFA daily.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20191128)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20191128)
n_sub <- 200

cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  SOFA = pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n_sub, mean = 12, sd = 4)), 2), 22),
  TBILI = 17.1
)
summary(cohort$SOFA)
```

# Simulation

Micafungin 100 mg once daily for 7 days, each dose infused over 1 h (the
labelled infusion time; the paper does not state it). Observations every
0.25 h on the `central` compartment.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Gastine_2019_micafungin")

dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = seq(0, 144, by = 24)) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 100, dur = 1, cmt = "central")
obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = seq(0, 168, by = 0.25)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")

events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, returnType = "data.frame")
sim <- sim |>
  mutate(
    day = pmin(floor(time / 24) + 1, 7),
    tad = time - 24 * (day - 1)
  )
```

# Typical-value covariate effects

The three covariate effects act on the typical clearance and central volume as
below. The linear SOFA effect keeps clearance positive across the observed
range (at SOFA 22 it is 0.76 times the SOFA-12 value).

```{r typical-values}
th <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta
cov_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(SOFA = c(2, 6, 10, 11, 12, 16, 22), bili_mgdl = c(1, 5)) |>
  mutate(
    CL = exp(th[["lcl"]]) * (1 + th[["e_sofa_cl"]] * (SOFA - 12)) *
      (1 + th[["e_tbili_cl"]] * (bili_mgdl > 4)),
    Vc = exp(th[["lvc"]]) * (1 + th[["e_sofa_vc"]] * (SOFA > 10))
  )
stopifnot(
  abs(cov_grid$CL[cov_grid$SOFA == 12 & cov_grid$bili_mgdl == 1] - 1.56) < 1e-12,
  abs(cov_grid$Vc[cov_grid$SOFA == 11][1] / cov_grid$Vc[cov_grid$SOFA == 10][1] - 0.692) < 1e-12
)
cov_grid |>
  mutate(CL = signif(CL, 3), Vc = signif(Vc, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "SOFA score" = SOFA,
    "Bilirubin (mg/dL)" = bili_mgdl,
    "Typical CL (L/h)" = CL,
    "Typical Vc (L)" = Vc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical clearance and central volume across the covariate range.")
```

# Replicate published figures

## Concentration versus time after dose (Figures 2 and 5)

Figure 2 plots the observed concentrations against time after the last dose
and Figure 5 the prediction-corrected VPC: the observed median falls from about
4.3 mg/L at 1 h after the dose to about 1.2 mg/L at 24 h, with the 95th
percentile near 7.5 mg/L at the peak. The simulated percentiles over days 2-7
are shown below; Figure 5 is prediction-corrected and pools all days, so the
comparison is visual.

```{r fig-vpc}
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(day >= 2, tad > 0) |>
  group_by(tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = median(sim),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Micafungin (mg/L)",
    title = "Replicates Figure 5 of Gastine 2019",
    caption = "Simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles, days 2-7, 100 mg once daily."
  )
```

## Concentration versus SOFA score (Figure 6)

Figure 6 shows concentrations rising with the SOFA score (the observed median
goes from about 1.6 mg/L at SOFA 5 to about 2.7 mg/L at SOFA 19), the
consequence of the lower clearance and lower central volume in the sicker
patients.

```{r fig-sofa}
sim |>
  filter(day >= 2, tad > 0) |>
  group_by(SOFA) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = median(sim),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(SOFA)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  labs(
    x = "SOFA score",
    y = "Micafungin (mg/L)",
    title = "Replicates Figure 6 of Gastine 2019",
    caption = "Simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles, days 2-7."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

Daily AUC0-24 for each simulated subject on days 1-7.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  transmute(id, time, Cc, treatment = "100 mg once daily")
dose_df <- dose_rows |>
  transmute(id, time, amt, treatment = "100 mg once daily")

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = seq(0, 144, by = 24),
  end = seq(24, 168, by = 24),
  auclast = TRUE,
  cmax = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_day <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  mutate(day = end / 24)
```

## Comparison against published values

The paper reports no NCA table. Figure 7 gives the post-hoc daily AUC0-24
divided by the C. albicans MIC of 0.016 mg/L as boxplots per study day. The
medians, digitised from the figure and multiplied by 0.016, are the reference
below. Figure 9 (C. parapsilosis, MIC 2 mg/L) gives the same AUCs to within
digitisation error (day 3-5 medians of about 33, i.e. 66 mg*h/L). The study
population shrank from 36 patients on day 1 to 7 on day 7, so days 6-7 rest on
few patients and are shown for completeness only.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~day, ~auclast,
  1, 3200 * 0.016,
  2, 4000 * 0.016,
  3, 4150 * 0.016,
  4, 4250 * 0.016,
  5, 4250 * 0.016,
  6, 4050 * 0.016,
  7, 3400 * 0.016
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_day |> select(day, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  reference = published,
  by = "day",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Median daily AUC0-24: simulated vs digitised from Gastine 2019 Figure 7 (AUC/MIC x 0.016 mg/L). * marks rows differing by >20%."
)
```

Two checks pin the model against Figure 7. The steady-state AUC (days 3-5)
depends on the typical clearance at the cohort's SOFA scores, so it tests the
centring of the linear SOFA effect: with the effect centred on the median of
12 the simulated median lies close to the digitised 66-68 mg*h/L, whereas an
uncentred effect (`1 - 0.024 x SOFA`) would give a SOFA-12 clearance of
1.11 L/h and a steady-state AUC near 90 mg*h/L (+33%). The ratio of the day-1
to the day-4 AUC depends mainly on the distribution kinetics and the
accumulation rather than on the covariates, so it tests the structural
parameters.

The simulated medians sit 5-8% below the digitised steady-state values and the
day-1 AUC 14% below. Three things separate the two sides and set the 15%
tolerance used below: the figure medians are digitised (about +/-3%); the
virtual cohort holds bilirubin below the 4 mg/dL threshold, whereas any study
patient above it had a 21% lower clearance and a higher AUC; and Figure 7
summarises post-hoc AUCs of a shrinking set of patients (36 on day 1, 24 on
day 4, 7 on day 7), so the day-to-day ratio also reflects who remained on
therapy. The day-7 box (7 patients) is not used in the checks. The uncentred
SOFA reading stays well outside the tolerance.

```{r nca-check}
auc_med <- nca_day |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  group_by(day) |>
  summarise(auc = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

ss_sim <- mean(auc_med$auc[auc_med$day %in% 3:5])
ss_pub <- mean(published$auclast[published$day %in% 3:5])
ratio_sim <- auc_med$auc[auc_med$day == 1] / auc_med$auc[auc_med$day == 4]
ratio_pub <- published$auclast[published$day == 1] / published$auclast[published$day == 4]

data.frame(
  check = c("Median AUC0-24, days 3-5 (mg*h/L)", "Day-1 / day-4 median AUC0-24"),
  published = signif(c(ss_pub, ratio_pub), 3),
  simulated = signif(c(ss_sim, ratio_sim), 3)
) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Centring of the SOFA effect: centred lands within a few percent, the
  # uncentred reading would be about +33%.
  abs(ss_sim / ss_pub - 1) < 0.15,
  # Accumulation from day 1 to steady state (structural parameters).
  abs(ratio_sim / ratio_pub - 1) < 0.15
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Centring of the linear SOFA effect on clearance.** The paper prints only
  'a linear decrease in clearance with a factor of 0.024 per score point' from
  the PsN stepwise covariate modelling. The PsN linear form
  `CL = TVCL x (1 + theta x (SOFA - median))` is used, centred on the Table 1
  median of 12. The steady-state AUCs of Figure 7 support the centred reading
  and exclude the uncentred one (see the check above).
* **Reference groups of the categorical effects.** The Results describe the
  SOFA > 10 group as having a 30.8% lower central volume and the bilirubin
  > 4 mg/dL group a 21.1% lower clearance; the Table 2 typical values are
  therefore taken to apply to SOFA <= 10 (Vc) and bilirubin <= 4 mg/dL (CL).
* **Bilirubin units.** The paper's threshold is 4 mg/dL; the model's `TBILI`
  column is in umol/L and is divided by 17.1 inside the model.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports the IIVs as percentages without a definition;
  they are converted with the exact log-normal relation
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.
* **IIV correlations.** The Results state that a full covariance matrix was
  estimated for the three random effects, but the covariances are not reported,
  so the etas are independent here. Simulated variability of parameter
  combinations (for example AUC with correlated CL and Vc) may therefore
  differ from the original fit.
* **Residual error.** Table 2 reports 'Proportional residual Error (%)' as
  0.257, while the IIV rows of the same column are printed as percentages
  (25.9, 70, 48.9). It is read as a proportional SD of 25.7%; the spread of the
  observations around the individual predictions in Figure 4A agrees with this
  reading rather than with a variance of 0.257 (an SD of 51%).
* **Infusion duration.** Not stated in the paper; the 1 h labelled infusion
  time is used. The day-1 samples are timed 'post application' and the later
  peaks 'one hour after infusion'.
* **Time-varying covariates.** SOFA and bilirubin were time-varying in the
  study (SOFA re-scored daily). The model accepts time-varying values, but the
  virtual cohort above holds them constant, and the cohort's SOFA distribution
  is assumed (normal, mean 12, SD 4, truncated to 2-22) because only the median
  and range are reported.
* **Bilirubin distribution.** Not reported; the cohort holds bilirubin at
  1 mg/dL. Patients above 4 mg/dL in the study would have raised the observed
  AUCs of Figure 7 somewhat relative to this cohort.
* **Published weight range.** Table 1 gives 49.9-162 kg and the Results text
  49.4-162 kg; the table value is recorded in the model metadata.
* No erratum was found for the article (search of the publisher page and
  PubMed, 2026-11-26).
